headline: Profit surges as costs ease and buybacks shrink share count
summary_short: Credit Acceptance posted Q2 FY2026 net income of $135.9M (+55.5% y/y) and diluted EPS of $12.66 (+70.6% y/y), as a $21.4M drop in operating expenses and a $13.4M decline in credit-loss provisions offset roughly flat revenue of $587.4M.
summary_long: Net income rose 55.5% y/y to $135.9M ($12.66 diluted EPS, +70.6%) as operating expenses fell 13.8% ($21.4M) — mainly the absence of a $23.4M year-ago legal contingent loss — and credit-loss provisions fell 7.8% ($13.4M) on smaller forecast-change charges. Interest expense fell 9.1% on lower average and cost of debt. Revenue was roughly flat at $587.4M (+0.6% y/y) as a modest rise in finance-charge yield offset a 1.0% decline in Consumer Loan unit volume; monthly volume returned to y/y growth in June and July. The company repurchased 262,963 shares (2.5% of shares outstanding) for $141.4M and held $1.4 billion of liquidity (cash plus undrawn revolver capacity) at quarter-end. No forward guidance was given.

drivers.explanation: CEO cites continued progress across the business driven by improved profitability, strengthening origination trends, and momentum across the dealer network, with a focus on profitable growth and disciplined capital allocation.
